questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have often visited Italy but always wanted to learn the language and get to know the lifestyle and culture more than what is possible on vacation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy. In Italy l'informazione non informa. It is almost impossible to know what to do, the good thing is in Italy there are no hard (or soft) deadlines. Everything works out in the end

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. I had access to a virtual hub where a woman could answer questions. Unfortunately she gave me wrong information about some of my courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had an apartment cancelled one month before going, so for me it was not easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't live in the northern part of Bologna outside of the city walls. It is fairly sketchy at night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to make a zoom call to register my presence in the city.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, not a lot of help. I had access to some zoom calls, but they didn't know a lot about basic questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end it worked out, but it was a nightmare. Courses was approved, then cancelled with no communication. OLA process unnecessarily complicated. In Bologna, classes are not fixed until you have it in your OLA and you have taken the exam.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask local students about courses, because the workers don't know what they are talking about a lot of the time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level varied enormously between courses. Risk management was ridiculously easy, while Decisions and Investments was incredibly difficult, for example.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of classes are 3 hours long with no breaks and no powerpoint (or maybe 5 slides). These type of classes are ineffective and uninteresting.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Riske management; Decisions and investments; Business models in creative industries; International economics and trade; machine learning for economists

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None of the courses I took.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I got a bike stolen, and I went to the hospital with a leg injury where I was charged 1200 DKK for an x-ray and a scan of my leg.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was way more expensive that I had imagined. I would say a lot of groceries are roughly as expensive here as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have not heard about any non-academic opportunities at the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bologna is in my opinion not a great city, so get out of the city as often as possible. Lots of fast trains to other cities, but buy tickets like at least a month in advance, because then it is pretty cheap, and otherwise it is fairly pricy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Medium I would say, but I think it is a very subjective experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just do it. Italians are very friendly, and in my experience the students are perfectly fine with speaking English and help translating for you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There are no systems. They make up complicated systems ad hoc for each individual situation. No two exams are alike. No one makes plans more than an hour in advance.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and openness of Italians

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Bologna is an extremely liberal city, if that is you that's great, but if you are the type of person who likes to wear a white shirt, reconsider your choice. 2) Be part of a club (like a dance class for example). It is a great way to meet locals. 3) Don't stay at the social hub or anywhere else in Bolognina. Try to get a place with the city walls in the southern part.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I have covered most things already.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The italian friends I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I really did not like the city, so coming to terms with that, I guess.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
